page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance. It is powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 4 vCPUs, which map to 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 15.0 GB of RAM, translating to 3.75 GB of memory per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 45 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the n1-standard-4 sits in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance scored 1107.78 and multi-core scored 2904.55, both placing in the bottom 25%. Geekbench results align with this, showing a single-core score of 927.0 and a multi-core score of 2044.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 161.64 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 25.29 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic operations via Passmark encryption scored 1349.62, and static web serving throughput reached 2.46 GB/sec.

As an older-generation instance family, the n1-standard-4 offers a balanced resource allocation but exhibits lower performance density compared to newer architectures. It is best suited for light general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, development environments, or small-scale database operations where high-throughput compute is not a primary requirement. The absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs limits its utility for high-performance storage-bound applications or intensive machine learning tasks, though it can handle basic low-parameter LLM inference, achieving 59.16 tokens/sec on a 135M model.
